annotation.interpretation_a: A packet is 'sufficiently long' if it contains enough data to determine the version being used, even if the payload is undecryptable.
annotation.interpretation_b: A packet is 'sufficiently long' if it meets a minimum length requirement (e.g., at least the size of the QUIC header) to prevent denial-of-service attacks, regardless of whether the version can be determined.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'sufficiently long' is vague and lacks a concrete definition. This allows for multiple interpretations of what constitutes a packet being 'sufficiently long' to trigger the sending of a Version Negotiation packet. Without a specific length or criteria, implementations could differ on how they handle short packets from unknown versions.
annotation.missing_information: The definition of 'sufficiently long' is missing. A concrete length or criteria is needed to avoid ambiguity in implementation.
